short: The Antikythera Mechanism was a complex ancient Greek analogue computer used to predict astronomical positions and eclipses.
full:
Dating to around 150 BCE, the Antikythera Mechanism was discovered in 1901 amidst a Roman-era shipwreck off the coast of the Greek island of Antikythera. This astonishingly intricate device consists of at least 30 interlocking bronze gears housed in a wooden box, operated by a hand crank.

The mechanism calculated the movements of the sun, the moon, and the known planets, predicting eclipses and tracking the four-year cycle of the ancient Olympic Games. Its sophisticated gear trains, including an epicyclic gear system, demonstrate a level of mechanical engineering that was previously thought not to exist until the development of astronomical clocks in 14th-century Europe, fundamentally altering our understanding of ancient Greek technology.
